title: Organization-Level Credit Limit and Consolidated Billing — Physician Client Accounts
content:
**Statement.** For Physician Client Accounts, the credit limit applies to the organization, not to a single location: the sum of the client balances of all the organization's open accounts is compared with the credit limit of its account class. When the class provides consolidated billing across locations, all locations receive one client invoice per period and a payment is applied to the oldest unpaid period across locations; otherwise each account is invoiced and paid separately.

## The organization balance

- The **client balance** of an account is what the organization owes the laboratory for client-billed tests on that account. Billed tests and late fees add to it; payments and credit memos reduce it; the balance shown on the account is the running total.
- The **organization balance** is the total of the client balances of every account of the same organization that is not closed: accounts in pending setup, active accounts and accounts on credit hold all count; closed accounts do not.
- That organization balance, never the balance of one location alone, is what is compared with the class's credit limit.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

An organization holds four accounts of one class, with a class credit limit taken here as USD 15000.00:

| Location | Status | Client balance | Counted in the organization balance |
|---|---|---|---|
| Location A | Active | USD 6200.00 | Yes |
| Location B | Active | USD 5400.00 | Yes |
| Location C | Credit hold | USD 4100.00 | Yes |
| Location D | Closed | USD 900.00 | No |

The organization balance is USD 6200.00 plus USD 5400.00 plus USD 4100.00, a total of USD 15700.00, which is above the USD 15000.00 limit, although no single location is above it. The closed account's USD 900.00 does not enter the total.

## Invoicing and payment across locations

| The account class provides consolidated billing across locations | Client invoices each period | Where a payment goes |
|---|---|---|
| Yes | One client invoice for all of the organization's locations | To the oldest unpaid period across locations |
| No | Each account receives its own client invoice | Each account is paid separately |

**Illustration (hypothetical).** In a class with consolidated billing, an organization whose oldest unpaid period across its locations is February and which also has March unpaid has its payment applied to the February period; in a class without consolidated billing, a payment made for one location's invoice settles that account only.
